part.text: {"reframes":[{"bottleneck":"The hypothesized ~25% chemistry-dependent error floor is a systematic force-field bias: more molecules, more replicas, or longer trajectories only re-measure the same bias at higher precision, so compute past ~48 molecules buys more of the same.","assumption":"The quantity scored against measurement must be each molecule's absolute viscosity and thermal conductivity.","reframe":"Change the measured quantity from absolute properties to paired differences: compute Δη and Δλ between molecule pairs with an identical protocol, where shared systematic error partially cancels, and score sign agreement against measured differences. Compute then buys correct ordering decisions rather than absolute accuracy.","question":"For molecule pairs whose measured viscosities differ by at least 15%, what fraction have sign(Δη_simulated) = sign(Δη_measured) when both legs use the same LOPLS-AA Green-Kubo protocol?","measure":"20 molecule pairs spanning 1–50 mPa·s from the reference set, 2 replicas × 5 ns per leg (200 ns total), count sign agreement of simulated vs measured viscosity differences. Rough cost $35 (about 2 machine-hours at the plan's throughput), done before scaling further.","compute_after":"More compute adds pairs and resolves near-tie pairs with extra replicas, directly improving decision accuracy at ranking boundaries instead of re-measuring a fixed bias.","exact":"Sign agreement = fraction of the 20 pairs where the simulated viscosity difference has the same sign as the measured difference, with per-leg η from the standard Green-Kubo integral at 40 °C.","expected":"Sign agreement ≥ 0.85 for pairs separated by ≥15% measured difference, even while absolute per-molecule error remains ~25%, showing the floor is largely common-mode.","fails_if":"Sign agreement ≤ 0.6 on well-separated pairs, meaning the error is molecule-specific noise rather than shared systematic bias, so differencing buys nothing.","closest_prior":"Ogbomo's 8-molecule study compared absolute simulated vs measured values only [s_ogbomo_md]; no paired-difference error cancellation has been tested on this set [s_ogbomo_db]."},{"bottleneck":"Green-Kubo viscosity and thermal conductivity converge slowly, so most of the $940 budget buys statistical averaging of a quantity whose accuracy is capped by the force field; the unit of work (30 ns of transport-coefficient sampling per molecule) is the most expensive way to obtain a ranking signal.","assumption":"The screening quantity must be the transport coefficient itself, estimated by Green-Kubo.","reframe":"Change the unit of work: screen with self-diffusion from the Einstein relation (converges roughly an order of magnitude faster than Green-Kubo viscosity) plus density, and reserve expensive Green-Kubo runs for survivors of a funnel over all 835 molecules — but only after checking the proxy actually tracks measured viscosity.","question":"Across 40 molecules spanning the reference set's chemistry classes, does the Spearman rank correlation between simulated self-diffusion coefficient and measured viscosity exceed |ρ| = 0.8?","measure":"40 molecules, one 2-ns replica each for mean-squared-displacement slope and density (80 ns total), compute Spearman ρ between D_sim and measured η at 40 °C. Rough cost $15, under one machine-hour.","compute_after":"If the proxy holds, each additional dollar buys funnel depth — cheap D screening on hundreds of molecules, Green-Kubo only on the top slice — so compute changes which candidates advance rather than polishing a capped estimate.","exact":"Spearman ρ between D_sim (Einstein MSD slope, 40 °C, LOPLS-AA) and measured η across the 40 molecules, with a per-class breakdown for alkanes vs esters.","expected":"|ρ| ≥ 0.8 overall and ≥ 0.7 within the ester class, sufficient to justify a two-stage screen where Green-Kubo is spent on ≤ 20% of candidates.","fails_if":"|ρ| < 0.5 overall or within any major class, meaning diffusion is not an informative proxy for viscosity here and the funnel would misdirect the expensive runs.","closest_prior":"Ogbomo ran Green-Kubo only on 8 molecules [s_ogbomo_md]; the 835-molecule reference set has no validated cheap-proxy screening stage [s_ogbomo_db]."},{"bottleneck":"The objective is global rank agreement over the whole benchmark, and the force field is held fixed; that combination guarantees the error floor caps the metric no matter how many molecules are added, and the plan's scalar bias correction is applied after the fact rather than learned.","assumption":"The force field must stay fixed, and success means a single global rank correlation across all benchmark molecules.","reframe":"Change the objective to a yes/no decision — is candidate X better than the incumbent coolant on both η and λ? — and unfix the field minimally by learning a class-conditional correction (per chemistry class, linear in carbon number) jointly with the benchmark, with compute allocated adaptively to molecules nearest the decision boundary.","question":"Can a class-conditional linear correction fit on 30 molecules with known measurements reduce held-out viscosity error below 15% and raise better/worse-than-incumbent decision accuracy above 90% on 20 held-out molecules?","measure":"Run 22 new molecules (reusing the published 8 for the fit set) at 6 replicas × 5 ns (~660 ns), fit per-class slope/intercept corrections on 30, evaluate held-out MAPE and decision accuracy on 20. Rough cost $110 (about 7 machine-hours).","compute_after":"Further compute buys boundary resolution: extra replicas and extra molecules are spent only where the classification is uncertain, so more compute moves candidates across the decision line instead of shrinking error bars on a capped global rank.","exact":"Held-out viscosity MAPE after applying the class-conditional correction, and decision accuracy = fraction of 20 held-out molecules correctly classified as better or worse than the incumbent on both η and λ.","expected":"Held-out error < 15% and decision accuracy ≥ 0.9 with the correction explaining most of the chemistry-dependent bias (correction R² > 0.7).","fails_if":"Residual held-out error stays above 25% with correction R² < 0.3, i.e., no class structure to the bias, meaning the error is irreducible per-molecule noise and neither correction nor boundary-focused compute can help.","closest_prior":"The plan's own bias-correction step treats error as a single scalar [s_ogbomo_res]; no class-conditional or decision-threshold framing appears in [s_ogbomo_md] or [s_ogbomo_db]."}]}
